title: Delta-ledger commit protocol for optimistic streaming metering
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: Customers have reported surprising charges or missing credits when a streaming session experiences optimistic mid-stream edits, client-side retries, or speculative decoding. Current ledgering assumes linear, finalized fragments; in practice fragments can be reordered, retracted, or merged by proxy layers, causing double-credits, orphaned provisional debits, or delayed refunds. This ticket designs and implements a delta-ledger commit protocol intended to make optimistic streaming metering deterministic, idempotent, and auditable while preserving low end-to-end latency.

Goal: Introduce a lightweight commit/abort protocol for per-session delta ledgers that supports optimistic provisional debits for in-flight fragments and a deterministic finalization path that either converts provisionals to settled credits or reclaims them without customer-visible overcharge. The protocol must be resistant to client reconnects, partial upstream failures, proxy merges, and mid-session model swaps.

Key concepts introduced: epoch_id (per-stream generation), fragment_seq (monotonic fragment sequence as observed by the initial groomer), provisional_debit entries (short-lived until commit), commit_markers (signed by server runtime with idempotency token), and reclamation windows (timeboxed automatic rollbacks for orphaned provisionals). The ledger stores delta records (append-only) with stable canonicalization rules to avoid duplicate token counting when fragments are retransmitted or merged.

Non-goals: This does not replace long-term billing reconciliation/audits; it's aimed at reducing transient incorrect charges and making online billing invariant checks stronger. We also do not change customer-facing quotas in this iteration (quota enforcement continues to use conservative token tallies until final commit).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Provisional debits can be created for in-flight fragments and are visible in per-session telemetry. 2) Commit_markers convert provisionals into settled debits atomically in the ledger; observing a commit must make final token tallies stable and deterministic. 3) Retransmits/duplicates do not double-charge: replaying the same fragment_seq with same idempotency token results in no additional settled debits. 4) If a session ends without commit, provisionals are reclaimed after configurable reclamation window and marked in audit log. 5) End-to-end e2e test demonstrating client reconnect + fragment merge yields same final billed tokens as a clean session replay. 6) Dashboard surfaces provisional vs settled token split for at least 30 days of retention. 7) Backfilling tool can reconcile ledgers where commit markers were lost due to region failover.
implementation_notes:
High-level design: implement a delta-ledger service shim that sits between the runtime request fan-in and the metering aggregator. The shim exposes 3 operations: create_provisional(fragment_meta), commit_epoch(epoch_id, commit_token), and reclaim_provisionals(epoch_id). Each provisional record includes: session_id, epoch_id, fragment_seq, token_estimate, validator_hash (prompt+kvcache-fingerprint), and idempotency_token. The commit operation atomically transitions matching provisionals to settled entries using optimistic concurrency (compare-and-append on epoch commit index). To avoid an unbounded open provisional state, reclamation is time-boxed and driven by background sweeper with exponential backoff and circuit-breaker on high reclaim volumes.

Edge-cases & tradeoffs: 1) Merge semantics: when a proxy merges fragments, we normalize by taking canonical fragment_seq assigned by first-seen groomer; merged fragments must reference original fragment_seq list in metadata to allow dedupe. 2) Client-driven retries with different content: validator_hash prevents accepting a different payload as same provisional; such variations create new provisional unless an explicit replace operation is performed. 3) Cost of provisional storage: provisionals are compacted into pointer records after commit to reduce storage. 4) Quota enforcement remains conservative: provisionals don't increment quota counters until commit to avoid quota exhaustion from speculative branches. This favors availability at the cost of stricter quota enforcement later.

DB model: append-only delta table (epoch_id + fragment_seq as primary composite string key), provisional flag, settled_flag, created_at, reclaimed_at, metadata_blob (small). Must support efficient range scans by session_id and reclamation by epoch creation time. Consider RocksDB or Dynamo style key-value store for hot paths; use Postgres for archival and audit queries.

API & runtime hooks: runtime generates idempotency_token per fragment, includes fragment_seq and epoch_id in attach header. Gateway proxies must preserve these headers. SDKs updated to surface provisional state in event stream (provisional_ack, commit_ack).
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (canary region): Enable delta-ledger shim for 5% of streaming sessions in us-east-1 with 'opt-in' header from SDK. Monitor provisional-to-settled conversion rates, reclaim frequency, and latency tail. Phase 2: Gradually increase to 50% after 2 weeks and run dedicated billing-simulation job to ensure no more than 0.1% variance vs current accounting. Phase 3: Full enable with fallback to legacy ledger on detected discrepancies >0.5% during a 24h window. For enterprise customers that require strict accounting, expose a flag to force immediate commit-on-send.

Rollback: Toggle off shim at router and drain provisionals by triggering reclamation sweeper; if faster rollback needed, convert remaining provisionals to settled with a special force_commit which logs a high-severity audit event.
test_plan: Unit tests for provisional lifecycle: create -> idempotent-create -> commit -> duplicate-commit no-op -> reclaim. Integration tests simulating: intermittent network with reconnects, proxy-merge scenario (two fragments merged into one), model-handoff mid-session, and client-side content mutation on retry. Add a chaos test that kills the delta-ledger process mid-commit and validates eventual consistency after restart. Add e2e experiment comparing billed tokens for 1M simulated sessions under new vs legacy ledgers and assert <0.1% discrepancy. Include fuzzing harness for sequence ID gaps and out-of-order fragment arrivals.
observability: Expose metrics: provisional_count_total, provisional_age_seconds_histogram, provisional_to_settled_ratio, reclaim_rate, commit_latency_p50/p95/p99, duplicate_replay_detected, forced_reclaim_count. Add log context: session_id, epoch_id, fragment_seq, idempotency_token. Create dashboard tile in Console under 'Metering -> Delta-Ledger' showing provisional vs settled tokens, top reclaiming sessions, and correlation with gateway errors. Create an alert: reclaim_rate > 0.2% sustained over 10m triggers pager. Instrument tracing spans for create_provisional and commit_epoch with baggage for token estimates.
